stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{10 x}{\left(x^{2} + 10\right)^{2}} \) and \( a_n = f(n) \). State the conditions the integral test requires for the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), and use the test to determine whether the series converges or diverges.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges, because f is positive, decreasing and continuous on \( [2, \infty) \) and \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{2}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \frac{5}{14} \).

worked_solution.text: On \( [2, \infty) \), f is positive, continuous because \( \left(x^{2} + 10\right)^{2} \) is positive there, and decreasing because \( f^{\prime}(x) = - \frac{10 \left(3 x^{2} - 10\right)}{\left(x^{2} + 10\right)^{3}} \) is negative there.
An antiderivative of f is \( - \frac{10}{2 x^{2} + 20} \).

\( \lim_{b\to\infty} \left[- \frac{10}{2 x^{2} + 20}\right]_{2}^{b} = \lim_{b\to\infty} \left(- \frac{10}{2 b^{2} + 20} - \left(- \frac{5}{14}\right)\right) \), and the first term approaches \( 0 \), so \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{2}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \frac{5}{14} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: limit notation on an improper integral

worked_solution.text: The integral converges, so by the integral test \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \) converges.
